stories.title: Trump rages at Alaska Democrat who reportedly recruited man with same name as Republican opponent – live
summary: Trump, citing New York Times report, says Mary Peltola’s actions to recruit a second Dan Sullivan ‘illegal’ and calls for her disqualification from US Senate race Peltola’s campaign reportedly recruited second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate raceSign up for the Breaking News US emailFor months, Mary Peltola’s campaign for Alaska’s Senate seat has denied any connection to a separate campaign launched by a man who, coincidentally, shares the exact same name as Peltola’s Republican opponent, Dan Sullivan.New reporting from the New York Times undercuts that claim.

The outlet reported, based on interviews, obtained text messages and legal filings, that the Peltola campaign had not only recruited Mr Sullivan (not the Republican), but had sought out a number of Dan Sullivans across the state for potential candidacy, as well as others who could peel votes away from Peltola’s main opponent.

stories.title: Coalition talks loom in Israel as Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs set to fall short of majority
summary: Projections show votes for Palestinian parties surged in a tight contest that drew highest turnout in decadesIsrael election – live updatesIsrael election: what we know so farAnalysis: Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscapeIsrael’s future hung in the balance on Wednesday as it became clear that Benjamin Netanyahu had lost his governing majority.

His political fate now depends on whether opposition Jewish parties are prepared to forge a common front with Palestinian parties, whose support surged in Tuesday’s elections.The leader of the Jewish opposition bloc, the retired general Gadi Eisenkot, appeared to rule out such a broad coalition in a premature declaration of victory overnight for what he called a “Zionist majority”.

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign reportedly recruited second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
summary: Republicans have condemned the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, calling it a ploy to split votesAlaska Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was behind an effort to recruit a challenger with almost the same name as the Republican US senator Dan Sullivan, both of whom will appear on the ballot in next week’s midterm elections, the New York Times reported on Wednesday.Republicans have condemned the presence in the race of two candidates named Dan Sullivan – one the two-term US senator, the second a retiree living in south-eastern Alaska with scant political experience – calling the newcomer a ploy by Democrats to cost the incumbent re-election by splitting his supporters.
